name: @chosengeneration/light-code-addon-linux
description: Light Code and Fire Code add-on: connect to Linux machines over SSH, run read-only commands and download files for investigation.

addon.description: Connect to Linux machines over SSH: read-only commands and file downloads for investigation.

settings.title: Linux
settings.description: Linux machines the assistant can connect to over SSH, to run read-only commands and download files for investigation. The assistant cannot change anything on a machine: every command it sends is checked against a read-only list first, and shown to you for approval like any other tool. The only thing written to a machine is by your own press of Set up SSH key.

fields.label: Also allow these programs
fields.help: Programs you know only read, beyond the built-in list. Any arguments are accepted for these, so add only ones that cannot change anything.

records.title: Machines
records.description: Give each machine a short label: it is what you and the assistant call it ("check the disk on prod-web-1").

fields.label: Label
fields.patternMessage: A label is letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore - up to 40, starting with a letter or digit.
fields.help: What you and the assistant call this machine.

fields.label: Password
fields.help: Kept in Light Code's secret storage. A wrong password is not retried, so the account is not locked.

fields.label: Private key file
fields.help: OpenSSH format, or a PuTTY .ppk from an older PuTTYgen (version 2, RSA). For a newer .ppk, load it into Pageant and choose Pageant, or save it from PuTTYgen with Conversions > Export OpenSSH key.

fields.label: Connect through (another machine's label)
fields.help: For a machine reached only through a jump host: add the jump host as a machine too, and put its label here.

fields.label: Notes for the assistant
fields.placeholder: What runs here, where its logs are
fields.help: Told to the assistant along with the machine list.

actions.label: Set up SSH key
actions.confirm: This signs in to {label} with its stored password and adds this PC's SSH key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys there (making the key first, in your .ssh folder, if there is none). Then it checks the key works and switches {label} to sign in with it. Nothing else on the machine is changed.
